name: Manikganj
tagline: Palaces, ghats and date-palm jaggery on the Dhaka–Aricha road — the grand Baliati estate, Nazrul's Teota, and the Paturia crossing on the Padma.

guide.bestTime: November to February for cool, dry weather — also the date-palm season, when the famous Hajari jaggery is made. Avoid the monsoon (June–September), when the river ghats flood and the Padma and Jamuna run high.
guide.gettingThere: About 65 km west of Dhaka via the Dhaka–Aricha Highway (N5), which runs ~36 km through the district; frequent buses from Gabtali (~1.5–2 hr). The highway ends at Paturia Ghat, where BIWTC ferries and launches cross the Padma to Daulatdia. There is no railway in Manikganj.
guide.difficulty: Easy. Close to Dhaka, well connected by road, with most sites clustered within an hour of Manikganj town. The river-ghat areas can be congested around Eid.

mustVisit.name: Baliati Zamindar Bari (Baliati Palace)
mustVisit.description: One of Bangladesh's grandest zamindar palaces — seven separate blocks with around 200 rooms on nearly six acres, enclosed by a wall with three lion-crested gateways and a rear dighi.
mustVisit.history: Founded by Gobinda Ram Saha, a salt merchant, and built through the 19th century by his sons and later family figures. The Department of Archaeology acquired it as protected property in 1987 and runs it as a museum, the renamed 'Baliati Palace'.

practical.hours: Daytime; closed on weekly government holidays

howToReach.transport: Bus/CNG from Manikganj town toward Saturia

mustVisit.bestTime: Daytime for the architecture and the museum
tips: Allow time to walk all seven palace blocks
The lion-crested gateways and rear dighi are highlights

mustVisit.name: Teota Zamindar Bari
mustVisit.description: A sprawling riverside zamindar palace of some 50+ rooms on the bank of the Jamuna, the family home of Pramila Devi, wife of the rebel poet Kazi Nazrul Islam.
mustVisit.history: Founded by Panchanan Chaudhuri, who rose through the tobacco trade, the estate is around three centuries old. Nazrul visited freely through his friendship with the Sen family; Pramila (née Pramila Sen) belonged to this household.

howToReach.transport: Bus toward Aricha/Shibalaya, then local transport

mustVisit.bestTime: Daytime for the palace and the Navaratna Temple
tips: The Navaratna Temple stands within the grounds
A good pairing with the nearby Paturia ghat

mustVisit.name: Navaratna Temple, Teota
mustVisit.description: A striking four-storey Hindu temple within the Teota estate, around 65–75 ft high, with unusually European detailing.
mustVisit.history: Built in 1857 and used for the family's Dol festival, the temple blends a classic Bengali tower form with colonial-era ornament. Stone inscriptions in the wider complex carry dates as early as 1702–03.

howToReach.transport: Bus toward Aricha/Shibalaya, then local transport

tips: See it together with the Teota palace
Note the European touches on a Hindu temple

mustVisit.name: Paturia Ferry Ghat
mustVisit.description: The major national ferry terminal and riverside viewpoint at the western end of the Dhaka–Aricha Highway, where ferries and launches cross the Padma to Daulatdia.
mustVisit.history: The western terminus of the N5 highway, Paturia handles a fleet of vehicle ferries and passenger launches on the ~3 km crossing to Daulatdia (Rajbari), the gateway to the country's southwest. It is a popular spot for sunset views and river snacks.

practical.hours: Daylight for views; ferries run through the day

howToReach.transport: Direct bus to Paturia along the N5

mustVisit.bestTime: Late afternoon for sunset over the river
tips: Try the riverside fried snacks while you wait
Crowds peak around Eid — go on an ordinary day

mustVisit.name: Matta Math (Mottar Moth)
mustVisit.description: A tall old temple-tower of around 50–60 ft on the bank of the Nital Dighi, just east of Manikganj town, carved with terracotta-style motifs.
mustVisit.history: Locally held to be over two centuries old and attributed to Zamindar Hem Sen, the math is a long-standing landmark of the Sadar area. Its exact founding date is uncertain.

howToReach.transport: Short rickshaw/CNG ride east of town

mustVisit.bestTime: Daytime for the carving and the dighi
tips: An easy add-on close to Manikganj town
Pair with a quiet stop by the Nital Dighi

mustVisit.name: Terasree 1971 Memorial
mustVisit.description: A Liberation War memorial at the village of Terasree, marking one of Manikganj's mass-grave sites of 1971.
mustVisit.history: Terasree was the scene of a 1971 massacre during the Liberation War; a memorial now stands at the site, with another near the Manikganj bus stand, in remembrance of those killed.
tips: A place of remembrance — visit quietly

specialties.name: Hajari Gur
specialties.description: A renowned, pale date-palm jaggery made for some two centuries in the Jhitka area of Harirampur — prized enough that its fame reached far beyond the district. Made fresh in winter.

specialties.name: Baul Gan
specialties.description: Manikganj is rich in folk song — Baul music is a regional hallmark, alongside older folk forms; the district's own slogan pairs 'Hajari Gur and Baul Gan' as the heart of local life.

foods.name: Hajari Gur
foods.description: The district's renowned pale date-palm jaggery from Jhitka, Harirampur — made fresh in winter and famous well beyond Manikganj.

foods.name: Khejur Gur (Patali & Jhola)
foods.description: Date-palm jaggery in solid (patali) and liquid (jhola) forms — a winter staple of the region.

foods.name: Pitha-Puli
foods.description: Traditional winter rice cakes made with the local date-palm gur.

foods.name: River Fish
foods.description: Fresh Padma and Jamuna fish, fried or in light curries at the riverside eateries near Paturia.

famousPeople.name: Khan Ataur Rahman
famousPeople.knownFor: Filmmaker, actor, music director and singer — born at Ramkantapur, Singair, Manikganj; director and composer behind Nawab Sirajuddaula, Sujon Sokhi and Abar Tora Manush Ho.

famousPeople.name: Hiralal Sen
famousPeople.knownFor: A pioneer of cinema in Bengal, often called the first Bengali filmmaker — his family roots are at Bagjuri, Manikganj, though he worked mainly from Kolkata.

famousPeople.name: Munier Chowdhury
famousPeople.knownFor: Linguist, playwright and martyred intellectual of 1971, whose family home is in Manikganj; remembered for the play Kabar and for his work on Bengali typography.

didYouKnow: Baliati Palace has seven separate palace buildings and around 200 rooms on nearly six acres — one of the largest zamindar complexes in Bangladesh — and has been state-protected by the Department of Archaeology since 1987.
Teota Zamindar Bari is the family home of Pramila Devi, wife of the rebel poet Kazi Nazrul Islam, who visited often through his friendship with the Sen family.
The Navaratna Temple at Teota, built in 1857, rises roughly four storeys and is unusually European in its styling for a Hindu temple.
Manikganj's Hajari Gur, a pale date-palm jaggery made for about two centuries in Jhitka, Harirampur, is so prized that the district's slogan pairs it with Baul gan as 'the real life of Manikganj'.
Manikganj has no railway — it relies on the Dhaka–Aricha Highway and the Paturia ferry ghat on the Padma, the gateway crossing to the country's southwest.
